title: Fixed expressions
subtitle: Expressions the exam builds its gaps on

slides.scenario: My sister saw I was struggling with my homework and offered to help.
He never says thank you to his mum. He just expects her to cook every day.
slides.meaning: to not value someone because they are always there

slides.scenario: Could you watch my bag for a minute while I buy a drink?
slides.meaning: to watch or look after something

slides.scenario: Going out tonight? No way. I have an exam tomorrow.
You've been looking at those two jackets for an hour. Which one do you want?

Saving a little every month is boring now, but you'll be glad later in life.
slides.meaning: over a long period of time

slides.scenario: Sorry I broke your pen. I didn't mean to, honestly!
We have to learn the whole poem for Friday, without looking at the book.
The moment they met, they knew they would be friends.
slides.meaning: immediately, the first time you see someone or something

slides.scenario: I'm living with my aunt until my parents find a new flat.
We argued for hours about where to eat, but finally we chose pizza.
I've read the instructions three times and I still don't understand them.

slides.scenario: If you don't listen carefully in class, you'll miss the important points.

slides.meaning: to try as hard as you can

slides.scenario: When you choose a university, think about the cost of living too.

slides.scenario: The engineer described clearly how the machine works.

slides.scenario: The bright poster made everyone stop and look.
